Modern.vision: A grocer whose third store is in the same neighbourhood as the first, with the same regular customers.

Paired they ground the brand in heritage household and neighbourhood vocabulary. Two-noun & paired naming follows the considered-modern grocery school (Bristol Farms, Erewhon's heritage spirit translated to small-format).
Modern.manifesto: Most modern grocery is built around 60,000-square-foot supermarkets. We started Larder & Lane to build the opposite — small neighbourhood stores under 5,000 square feet, with a curated catalog focused on what households actually use every week. The neighbourhood relationship is the work.
Modern.industrySummary: Grocery has consolidated around large-format supermarkets and rapid-delivery dark stores. Modern.competitorLandscape: Erewhon (erewhonmarket.com) plays the considered-modern grocery peer at premium. Bristol Farms (bristolfarms.com) holds the regional considered-grocery peer slot. Foodland (foodlandhawaii.com) sits in the regional independent peer position. Citarella (citarella.com) plays the heritage neighbourhood grocer peer reference. Modern.positioningStatement: Larder & Lane is a small-format modern neighbourhood grocer with a curated catalog of pantry staples, produce, and prepared foods.

Luxury.vision: A market whose 150th anniversary in 2062 is celebrated by the descendants of the customer families who shopped here in 1912.

Westbury is a real English place-name with a market-town register. The Market suffix places the brand firmly in the heritage independent grocer tradition.
Luxury.manifesto: Most premium grocery has been absorbed into supermarket chains. The Westbury Market has remained an independent single-location grocer since 1912, in continuous family operation through four generations. Custom hampers, special orders, and personal customer relationships are the practice. The store is a market, not a supermarket.
Luxury.industrySummary: Heritage independent grocers are a small but enduring tradition (Borough Market vendors, Fortnum & Mason, Eli's Manhattan, Citarella). There is space for a brand operating in this heritage with custom-order capabilities and multi-generational customer relationships.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Fortnum & Mason (fortnumandmason.com) is the heritage grocer reference at scale. Citarella (citarella.com) holds the heritage urban grocer peer slot. Luxury.positioningStatement: A heritage independent grocer operating one historic store since 1912 with a deep catalog of imported and artisanal goods and bespoke customer service.
Luxury.positioningRationale: We do not extend the market. The single historic store is the practice. Customer relationships span multiple generations of the customer family.

Minimal.mission: To sell fifty good pantry staples and keep selling them.
Minimal.vision: A pantry brand whose tenth-anniversary catalog is the same fifty items as its first.
coreValues: Plain — fifty items, fifty prices.
Direct — the catalog is the product.
Considered — every staple earns its place.
Minimal.brandNameRationale: Stock is the real grocery-trade word for shelf-held inventory — and the kitchen-trade word for the foundational broth used in cooking. Single archaic trade word, double meaning that grounds the brand in both retail and culinary contexts. Single-word naming follows the modern minimal grocery school (Brandless's spirit, Italic's pantry tier).
Minimal.manifesto: Most pantry brands expand into seasonal collections, gift bundles, and limited-edition flavours. We made Stock because the actual pantry is the same fifty items year after year — olive oil, vinegar, salt, pepper, beans, rice, flour, sugar, mustard. Stock sells those fifty. Minimal.industrySummary: Pantry brands pursue seasonal collections and flavour variants. There is real space for a minimal brand that strips the catalog to a permanent fifty items and refuses seasonal change.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Brandless (brandless.com, now defunct) was the closest peer in minimal pantry. Italic's pantry tier (italic.com) plays the modern peer reference. Corporate.brandDescription: Hampton Grocery Holdings operates a portfolio of grocery store brands across full-service supermarket, specialty grocery, and convenience-format categories.

• Multi-brand grocery store operations
• Shared supply-chain and procurement infrastructure
• Private-label product development across brands

Corporate.mission: To provide a serious operating platform for mid-tier grocery brands that want to keep their identity and outsource the operations.
Corporate.vision: A grocery operator whose portfolio brands grow under their own names because the supply chain and real estate are shared.
coreValues: Senior — partners deal with partners.
Operational — supply chain runs on schedule.
Reliable — predictable supply across brands.
Discreet — brand relationships stay private.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Hampton is a real American place-name common across the eastern United States with a heritage holding-company register. Grocery Holdings follows the multi-brand operator naming convention used in grocery (Albertsons Companies, Kroger Co., Ahold Delhaize structure). The pair reads as an institutional operator with multi-brand portfolio scale.
Corporate.manifesto: Hampton Grocery Holdings owns and operates a portfolio of grocery store brands. Each brand retains its identity, regional positioning, and customer relationships; we operate the shared supply chain, procurement, private-label development, and back office. The buyer is a grocery brand founder considering sale, a real-estate operator seeking single-vendor anchor tenant relationships, or an institutional investor holding grocery assets.
Corporate.industrySummary: Grocery has consolidated under a small number of large multi-brand operators (Kroger, Albertsons, Ahold Delhaize). The opening underneath is for a regional mid-tier multi-brand operator with deep supply-chain operations and the procurement-grade reliability real-estate operators and institutional investors require.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Albertsons Companies (albertsons.com) is the multi-brand grocery reference. Kroger (kroger.com) holds the multi-brand peer slot. Ahold Delhaize (aholddelhaize.com) sits in the international multi-brand peer position. Wakefern Food Corp (wakefern.com) plays the multi-banner cooperative peer reference. We belong in the regional mid-tier multi-brand grocery operator category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Hampton Grocery Holdings is a regional multi-brand grocery operator running shared supply chain, procurement, private-label development, and real-estate management across a portfolio of brands.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on shared supply-chain depth, private-label development capacity, and the operational reliability brand founders, real-estate operators, and institutional investors need.

Corporate.tagline: A portfolio of regional grocery operating companies.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Continental signals multi-region scope. Grocery Holdings positions the firm as an operator across multiple regional chains rather than a single brand.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate grocery is increasingly a roll-up game — private equity buying regional chains and consolidating distribution. The buyer is institutional capital, large suppliers, and the regional chain CEOs themselves.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Albertsons (albertsons.com) is the institutional peer. Ahold Delhaize (aholddelhaize.com) holds the multi-brand precedent. Cerberus Grocery investments set the PE-backed bar. We sit one tier below Albertsons with a sharper regional structure.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A multi-regional grocery operating group with independent chain brands.

targetAudience.primary: 45 to 65. Regional chain CEOs, supplier sales VPs, PE investment principals. Manage grocery portfolios above $1B revenue. Care about supplier terms, regional brand equity, and rollup execution.

Creative.tagline: A grocery built around what's actually in the cupboard.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Pantry is the household food-storage room — a domestic trade word. Project frames the brand as ongoing. The definite article gives the proper-noun register.
Creative.manifesto: Most grocery brands sell the weekly stock-up. The week-of-meals. The Pinterest-pantry. We made Snack Time because the truth about grocery shopping is that the best part is the chips, the drink, the small thing you bought because you wanted it. The brand is for the snack, the late-night fridge, the bag opened in the parking lot.
Creative.industrySummary: Grocery branding has been earnest, sustainability-led, and slightly preachy. There's room for a brand that's loud, warm, sticker-friendly, and serious about the small daily pleasure of food.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Trader Joe's (traderjoes.com) holds the playful-grocery peer position. Erewhon (erewhonmarket.com) sits at the lifestyle tier. Aldi (aldi.us) does the value-led middle. We sit warmer and funnier than any of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: A grocery brand that celebrates the snack, not the stock-up.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 45. Buys groceries twice a week. Likes the chips aisle. Tells friends about the brand by tagging them in a snack photo at 3 p.m.

dos: Make jokes about the chips aisle
Photograph customers eating the snacks
Talk to the snacker like a friend who'd share
donts: Photograph empty pantries with curated jars

Creative.tagline: A grocery brand built around what you actually cook.
Creative.brandDescription: The Weekly Box Co is a creative-led grocery brand shipping a curated weekly box of ingredients selected to match three planned meals, with recipes printed on the box itself.
Creative.scope:
The Weekly Box Co works across:
• Weekly subscription box of curated grocery ingredients
• Three planned meals per box with recipes printed on the packaging
• Direct relationships with farms and producers for box contents
• Quarterly published essays on home cooking and weekly meal planning
• Customer recipe-suggestion programme
Creative.mission: To make weekly grocery planning a finished decision delivered to the door.
Creative.vision: A grocery brand whose weekly box becomes the standard reference for home cooking rhythm.
coreValues: Warm — the box is for the household.
Specific — every box has three planned meals.
Considered — the chef-curator selects what's in season.
Literary — the writing about home cooking is part of the brand.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The Weekly Box is a phrase about the regular grocery delivery — the box that arrives once a week with what the household will cook. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school. Stands in the lineage of creative-led grocery and meal-kit brands (Hello Fresh's category translated to grocery, Misfits Market spirit).
Creative.manifesto: Most grocery shopping is decision fatigue extended over the week. We started The Weekly Box Co to compress the decision into one weekly delivery — a curated box of grocery ingredients selected to match three planned meals, with the recipes printed right on the box. The box arrives Tuesday; the cooking decisions are done.
Creative.industrySummary: Meal-kit services have consolidated around pre-portioned, sometimes pre-cooked deliveries. There is real space for a grocery-focused box service that delivers ingredients (not meal kits) selected to match planned recipes, with the recipes printed on the packaging.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Misfits Market (misfitsmarket.com) plays the closest peer in subscription grocery box. Imperfect Foods (imperfectfoods.com) holds the considered-modern peer slot. Hungryroot (hungryroot.com) sits in the curated-grocery-meal peer position. Daily Harvest (daily-harvest.com) plays the considered-meal subscription peer reference. We sit alongside Misfits Market with a stronger weekly-recipe focus.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Weekly Box Co is a grocery subscription brand shipping a curated weekly box of ingredients selected to match three planned meals with recipes printed on the box.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the weekly compression. One delivery. Three planned meals. The recipes are the box.

Subscribe to weekly recurring services.

Want grocery planning simplified.

Want recipes printed on the box.

Creative.tagline: Grocery delivery for the actual list.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Most grocery brands try to replace your shopping list with their algorithm. This one centers the list itself — the human document of what the household actually needs.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative grocery serves households who write a list, want the list filled, and don't want to be sold anything extra. The brand is warm, honest, and slightly funny — a friend with a car going to the store.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Instacart (instacart.com) holds the shopper-platform slot but feels corporate. Good Eggs (goodeggs.com) is the considered-grocery peer. Farmgirl Flowers (farmgirlflowers.com) sets the warm-DTC voice bar. We sit closer to Good Eggs in spirit.
Creative.positioningStatement: Grocery delivery that brings exactly what's on your list.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 50. Households who write a list before going to the store. Tip well. Send thank-you notes via the app. Care about the relationship with the shopper.
